minutes.headline: Planning Board approved a special permit and site plan for a home ground-mount solar array on Goodrich Street, with conditions.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board received OpenGov portal training from the building commissioner, then held a public hearing approving (with conditions) a site plan and special permit for a residential ground-mount solar array at 390 Goodrich Street, prompting discussion of the town's outdated solar bylaw. The board also covered MBTA Communities bylaw warrant timing, delayed responding to the Master Plan Steering Committee, and heard committee reports including early Municipal Building Design Committee thinking about reconfiguring Ritter Town Hall.

what_happened.line: The board closed the hearing and approved, with conditions, a special permit and site plan for a home ground-mount solar array at 390 Goodrich Street.
Conditions include posting a decommissioning bond before occupancy, sized to the array's removal cost, plus documentation of wiring and the utility interconnection agreement.
Board members said the town's solar bylaw is outdated and raised hiring a planner to update it.
The board agreed that MBTA Communities zoning language from its consultants should go on the town meeting warrant, ahead of an October 2 submission deadline.
The board put off responding to the Master Plan Steering Committee's request for feedback on the town's master plan.

why_it_matters: This sets the bonding and documentation conditions a homeowner installing a ground-mount solar array in Lunenburg can expect to meet.
The solar bylaw is described as outdated, so residents proposing solar projects may see zoning terms change before their own applications are heard.
MBTA Communities zoning language is headed for a town meeting warrant article, meaning residents will be asked to vote on it.
